changes.before:
BOTTOM LINE: An AI-driven clinical decision support intervention did not significantly reduce postoperative delirium or improve adherence to best practices among surgical patients with cognitive impairment.

- Study type: Pragmatic randomized controlled trial
- Population/setting: 7294 surgical patients with preoperative cognitive impairment at The Mount Sinai Hospital, New York City, from June 2023 to August 2024
- Intervention/exposure & comparator: AI-driven non-interruptive clinical decision support intervention versus routine perioperative care
- Primary endpoints: Incidence of postoperative delirium assessed with the 4 A's Test within seven days postoperatively
- Key results: No statistically significant difference in postoperative delirium incidence between intervention and control groups (35.1% vs 32.7%, P = .37); no significant difference in adherence to perioperative best practices (all P > .05).
- Limitations:
- Less than 20% of patients had documented delirium assessments
- Variability in routine postoperative delirium screening practices
- Limited ability to draw definitive conclusions about intervention effectiveness
- Why this matters: Effective strategies are needed to prevent postoperative delirium in cognitively impaired patients, but this AI-driven intervention did not demonstrate benefit in this setting.
